1soophe: A decided plan or a promise made right now?
1d0zyle: With **ir a + infinitive** you talk about something you decided before speaking: it's in your diary. _Este sábado voy a subir al volcán Pacaya_. You also use it when you see a sign right now: _Mira el cielo: va a llover_.
1uf2mmw: With the **simple future** you make a promise or an offer on the spot (_Tranquila, te mandaré las fotos_), a prediction with no sign in front of you (_Algún día viviré en Guatemala_) or a formal announcement, as in an email or on the radio (_El autobús saldrá a las seis_).
1apcnxw: Often both forms are possible. In conversation, above all in much of Latin America, **ir a** is the most frequent. The future sounds more like a promise, a written text or a distant dream.
16bky6l: Ask yourself: did I decide it before, or am I promising it now? Before → **voy a**. Now, to another person → **future**.
14omxm: Two futures, two points of view
1lj54yd: After **voy a** comes the infinitive. Use one form or the other, never both together.
9neb3: There are three pieces: **ir + a + infinitive**. Don't forget the **a**.
w6xk60: The regular future: the whole infinitive + an ending
uyi131: The future is easy to form: you don't remove anything. You take the **whole infinitive** (_visitar, volver, subir_) and add the ending. The endings are **the same** for -ar, -er and -ir.
1citst4: Every person has a written accent except **nosotros**: _visitaré, volverás, subirá, subiréis, visitarán_, but _volveremos_. The stress of the voice falls at the end of the word.
oegvm9: Without the accent, the word changes: _visitara_ or _llamara_ are not future forms. Always write the accent in _visitará_, _llamaré_.
1jsaswk: **Nosotros** is the only future form without a written accent.
6x1lpw: _Ayudé_ is past. With **mañana** you need the future: ayud**aré**.
1ksot5f: Ten verbs with a changed stem
1xmzegc: A small group of very frequent verbs changes its **stem**, but the endings don't change: _tendré, tendrás, tendrá…_
d2nfuj: There are three families. Some lose the vowel and add a **d**: _tener → tendr-_, _salir → saldr-_, _venir → vendr-_, _poner → pondr-_. Others just lose the vowel: _poder → podr-_, _saber → sabr-_, _haber → habr-_, _querer → querr-_. And two are very short: _hacer → har-_, _decir → dir-_.
1ccslyf: **Habrá** is the future of **hay**. That's why it is always singular: _habrá muchas personas_, never _habrán_.
ef3hod: Write the ten stems on a card and read it aloud three times: _tendr-, saldr-, vendr-, pondr-, podr-, sabr-, habr-, querr-, har-, dir-_.
7bbve8: Si + present, and the future afterwards
ynl1sg: For a real condition in the future, after **si** comes the **present**, not the future: _Si llueve, nos quedaremos en el hostal_. The consequence can be in the future or with **ir a**: _Si llueve, vamos a quedarnos_.
liy132: The order can change with no problem: _Nos quedaremos en el hostal si llueve_. When the sentence starts with **si**, add a comma.
pbv4ik: To recognise: sometimes the future doesn't talk about the future but about a **guess** about now: _—¿Dónde está Sergio? —Estará en el mercado_ (= he's probably at the market).
1iycsrv: First you choose between the two futures; then you form the regular future, the irregular stems and the sentence with **si**.

tabu29: The final beat of the future
sjrknv: In the future, the stressed syllable is **at the end**: _vi-si-ta-RÉ, vol-ve-RÁS, su-bi-RÁN_. That's why almost all forms have a written accent.
1vivbxb: Only **nosotros** has the stress on the second-to-last syllable: _vi-si-ta-RE-mos_. That's why it has no accent.
1ajyokf: This final beat helps you tell apart tenses that look alike: _llegará_ (future, stress at the end), _llegaba_ (past, stress on -GA-) and _llega_ (present).
1yjm6xm: The accent in the future marks the stress at the end: **llamaré, comerás, vivirán**. Without the accent, _llamare_ or _llamara_ are other forms. Nosotros never has it: **llamaremos**.
1d8xmc6: A clear beat at the end, as if the word ended in a jump.
1cway98: Two nosotros forms: no final beat.
